title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Complexe de co-Lie des groupes de t.m.', i.e. the co-Lie complex of groups of multiplicative type.

Setting. S is a base; M is a sheaf of abelian groups of finite type on S, locally constant or 'tordu' (twisted). G = D(M) = Hom(M, G_m) is the dual group of multiplicative type. The page writes 'réseau', but M must be allowed to have torsion. Otherwise G is a torus and the derived tensor product below is just M ⊗ O_S, so the statement has no content.

Step 1, canonical resolution (1.1). Grothendieck takes the canonical two-term flat resolution 0 → R → Z[M] → M → 0. Here Z[M] is the free abelian sheaf on the underlying set-sheaf of M, u([m]) = m, and R = Ker u. R is flat because it is a subsheaf of a torsion-free sheaf.

Step 2, dualising (1.2). Applying D gives 0 → G → T → T' → 0, with T = D(Z[M]) = G_m^M and T' = D(R). This resolves G by '(infinite-rank) tori'. Note that G_m^M is an infinite product, hence affine but not of finite type; this is the parenthetical about being 'relativement infinis'. Right exactness uses the fppf-local vanishing of Ext^1(M, G_m) for M of finite type.

Step 3, transitivity (1.3). The transitivity triangle for co-Lie complexes of a short exact sequence of flat groups, ℓ_{T'} → ℓ_T → ℓ_G →, is attributed to Mazur–Roberts. For tori the co-Lie complex is the module of invariant differentials: ω_T = Z[M] ⊗ O_S and ω_{T'} = R ⊗ O_S. Hence
ℓ^G ≃ [R ⊗ O_S → Z[M] ⊗ O_S] (degrees −1, 0) = M ⊗^L_Z O_S.
Example: G = μ_n gives ℓ = [O_S --n--> O_S].

Step 4, change of coefficients (1.4). If O_S is a Λ-algebra (for example Λ = Q or Z/n), associativity gives ℓ^G ≃ (M ⊗^L_Z Λ) ⊗^L_Λ O_S.

Continuation on the next page. For Λ = F_p the last tensor product is underived. If M comes by descent from a π-module M_0 via a Galois cover, so that M = f^*M_0 for f : S → B_π, then
ℓ^G ≃ f^*(M_0 ⊗^L F_p) ⊗ O_S.
This expresses the co-Lie complex in characteristic p through the two-term complex of π-representations [M_0 --p--> M_0], with H^0 = M_0/p and H^{-1} = M_0[p].

Purpose. The likely aim is to control deformations and obstructions of multiplicative-type groups, a test case for the Barsotti–Tate / crystals programme of 1970, by reducing ℓ^G to representation-theoretic data on B_π.
errors: The word 'réseau' is misleading. If M were a lattice, G would be a torus and ℓ^G ≃ M ⊗ O_S in degree 0, so the derived tensor product is only meaningful when M has torsion; M must be an abelian group (sheaf) of finite type, possibly twisted.

Minor gap: T = G_m^M is not of finite type, while the Mazur–Roberts / Illusie transitivity triangle is usually stated for groups locally of finite presentation. The formula ω_T = Z[M] ⊗ O_S, and the use of the triangle, need a limit argument (the cotangent complex commutes with filtered colimits of rings). The argument still works.
Surjectivity of T → T' (fppf) relies on the local vanishing of Ext^1(M, G_m), which is not stated.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard computation of the co-Lie complex of D(M), essentially the one in Illusie's Complexe cotangent II. Its only historical interest is that it documents Grothendieck working with Mazur–Roberts' transitivity triangle around 1970. No new result or overlooked connection.
transcription_corrections: Title should read 'Complexe de co-Lie des groupes de t.m.' (not 'cotic'/'cotangent'); t.m. = type multiplicatif.
'M un réseau sur S = gr. ab. de type fini sur S' is uncertain; the image more plausibly reads '= gr. ab. tordu sur S' (twisted constant abelian group).
'(c'est à dire relativement infinie...)' is probably '(c'est-à-dire relativement infinis...)', referring to infinite-rank tori.
In the line before (1.3) the first displayed symbol is a crossed-out 'ℓ_G'; then ℓ^G ≃ [ω_{T'} → ω_T] ≃ [R ⊗_Z O_S → Z[M] ⊗_Z O_S].
The previous page's transcription is a degraded duplicate of this page (Z^{(M)} = Z[M], α = u).
